moat_against: Hyperscaler DBaaS (DocumentDB, Cosmos DB) bundled with distribution and credits
Postgres + JSONB and open-source document stores commoditizing the model
Consumption pricing: revenue re-earned continuously, no contractual lock-in
SBC-funded talent model dilutes holders (share count +5.8%/yr)
CEO transition in progress (Desai departed; Ittycheria interim)
moat_for: Developer mindshare / default choice for document workloads
Data gravity: production apps are costly to re-platform
Atlas consumption model, net ARR expansion 122%
Multi-cloud portability hyperscaler-native DBs cannot match
Platform broadening (vector search, search) raising multi-feature adoption
moat_justification: De facto standard document database with real production-embedding switching costs and 122% net ARR expansion, but the document model is commoditizing: hyperscalers bundle rival DBaaS with distribution and credits, Postgres/JSONB covers more of the use case each year, consumption pricing gives no contractual lock-in, and Atlas growth has held ~29% rather than accelerating on the AI tailwind. No network effect; pricing power unproven.
name: MongoDB, Inc.
one_liner: Excellent growth franchise, moat 5/10, but owner's earnings turned positive only in the TTM window ($1.16/sh) against a $365.55 price — weighted IRR 3.3%, IV@15% $20.12; clears 15% only near ~$20.
